text: Make 'athena land --pr' work on repositories that allow only squash merges, as this one does (GitHub reports allow_squash_merge true; allow_merge_commit and allow_rebase_merge false). Sri chose this over enabling merge commits, so Athena works on any user's repository. Root cause of today's failures: squash merges break ancestry, so after one job lands, the local branch no longer descends from main and the next job's PR conflicts (PR #40 needed a hand rebuild of the landed commit on main, same tree and message, pushed with a lease). Three parts. (1) Read the allowed merge methods from the host and request one that is allowed; a squash's commit message carries the job's trailers in its last paragraph with exactly one Athena-Job, so 'athena check --history' passes on main. (2) After a squash lands, Athena brings the local branch onto main by itself: later landed jobs and records are rebuilt on top of the squash commit without losing any unlanded work, so the next 'athena land --pr' opens a clean PR. (3) Revise the merge-commit landing decision recorded by job 9h2j in docs/decisions.md and the design doc, citing Sri's choice. Test against a real local git repository.
